The proposed answer is correct.

**Reformulation.** Let $T = \mathbb{Z}_p^*\setminus S$, which is also symmetric. Then $\{x_1,\dots,x_{r+1}\}$ is a clique in $\text{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_p,S)$ exactly when it is an independent set in $\text{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_p,T)$. So we need the smallest symmetric $T$ with $\alpha(\text{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_p,T))\le r$, and $\text{ex}_{Cay} = p-1-\min|T|$.

**Construction.** Take $T=\{\pm1,\dots,\pm k\}$. This gives the $k$-th power of the $p$-cycle, whose independence number is $\lfloor p/(k+1)\rfloor$. This is at most $r$ iff $k\ge\lfloor p/(r+1)\rfloor$. Since $p$ is prime and $2\le r+1\le p-1$, $r+1$ does not divide $p$, so $\lfloor p/(r+1)\rfloor=\lfloor (p-1)/(r+1)\rfloor$. This yields $|S| = p-1-2\lfloor (p-1)/(r+1)\rfloor$.

**Checks on small cases.**
- $r=1$: the formula gives $0$, which is correct since $K_2$-free forces $S=\emptyset$.
- $r=2$ (triangle-free): $S$ must be a symmetric sum-free set. The formula gives $\lfloor (p+1)/3\rfloor$ or $(p-1)/3$ depending on $p \bmod 3$, matching the known maximum sum-free sizes. For example, $p=5\to 2$, $p=7\to 2$, $p=11\to 4$, $p=13\to 4$, all verified directly.
- $p=7$, $r=3$: $S=\{\pm1,\pm2\}$ gives clique number 3, so the value is $4$, matching the formula.
- $r=p-1$: $S$ cannot be all of $\mathbb{Z}_p^*$, and $p-1$ is even, so $|S|\le p-3$. The set $S=\mathbb{Z}_p^*\setminus\{\pm a\}$ attains $p-3$, so $\text{ex}_{Cay}(K_p,\mathbb{Z}_p)=p-3$. The boxed formula gives $p-1-2\cdot 1=p-3$, matching.

**Boxed expression.** For $1\le r\le p-2$, $\lfloor (p-1)/(r+1)\rfloor\ge 1$, so the $\max(1,\cdot)$ is inactive and the expression equals $p-1-2\lfloor (p-1)/(r+1)\rfloor$. For $r=p-1$ the $\max$ supplies the $1$ needed to give $p-3$. The "equivalently" clauses are consistent with this.

The lower bound (that no symmetric $T$ smaller than $2\lfloor p/(r+1)\rfloor$ works) is not proved here. It rests on the small cases above and on the match with the known sum-free results for $r=2$, which I take to be the established result for this problem.
